status: draft — first New Testament book, tier structure proposed and confirmed with the user 2026-08-07 before writing (Jesus gets a full independent manager tier per Gospel, matching the Aaron-in-Exodus-and-Leviticus precedent)
notes: First NT book — extends the OT schema with one addition: role:"law" tiers (established for Leviticus/Deuteronomy) are reused here for Jesus's major discourses (Sermon on the Mount, Parables of the Kingdom, Olivet Discourse, Great Commission), with deliveredBy:"jesus" and 'purpose' explaining what each teaches. NAMING COLLISION FLAGGED: Matthew 2's Herod ('Herod the king') is Herod the Great; Matthew 14's Herod ('Herod the tetrarch') is his son Herod Antipas, who executes John the Baptist — two different men, kept as herod_the_great (own tier) and herod_antipas (submanager under John the Baptist's tier, since his role in the book is entirely about John's death). Genealogy note: Jesus's earthly genealogy (Matthew 1:1-17, Abraham through Jesus in three sets of fourteen generations) is almost entirely OT figures already indexed in Genesis/Ruth/Samuel/Kings/Chronicles — not re-indexed here as individual characters, logged as a bulk reference in genealogyLists instead, with the four named women (Tamar, Rahab, Ruth, Bathsheba — unusual for a genealogy of this era to name women at all) flagged as a real textual feature. Jesus's own genealogy.father is set to null per the text's own account (Matthew 1:18-20 — conceived of the Holy Spirit); Joseph is his legal/adoptive father, not biological, and is described that way rather than listed as genealogy.father.

characters.name: Jesus Christ

verses.note: Conceived of the Holy Spirit; born to Mary, Joseph's betrothed wife
Baptized by John in the Jordan; the Spirit descends as a dove, a voice from heaven declares Him God's Son
Tempted by the devil forty days in the wilderness
The Sermon on the Mount

A sequence of healings and miracles — leper, centurion's servant, Peter's mother-in-law, the storm calmed, demoniacs, the paralytic, Matthew's own calling, the woman with the issue of blood, Jairus' daughter, two blind men
Teaches the Parables of the Kingdom
Feeds the five thousand
Walks on the water
Asks the disciples 'whom say ye that I am' — Peter's confession, 'Thou art the Christ'
The Transfiguration on the mountain
The triumphal entry into Jerusalem
Cleanses the temple
The Olivet Discourse
Institutes the Lord's Supper at the Last Supper
Agony in Gethsemane
Betrayed, arrested, tried before Caiaphas and Pilate
Crucified at Golgotha
Rises from the dead
Gives the Great Commission

funFacts: Matthew's Gospel is written with a strong pattern of Old Testament fulfillment — the phrase 'that it might be fulfilled which was spoken' recurs throughout, tying the birth narrative alone to at least five separate OT prophecies (Isaiah, Micah, Hosea, Jeremiah).

characters.name: John the Baptist

verses.note: Preaches repentance in the wilderness of Judaea, clothed in camel's hair, eating locusts and wild honey
Baptizes Jesus, initially protesting that he needs to be baptized by Him instead
From prison, sends disciples to ask Jesus 'Art thou he that should come?'
Beheaded by Herod Antipas at the request of Herodias' daughter, after condemning Herod's unlawful marriage

funFacts: Matthew's Gospel does not include the birth narrative of John the Baptist (his parents Zacharias and Elisabeth, found in Luke 1) — he simply appears as an adult preacher in chapter 3, so no genealogy is recorded here for this book specifically.

characters.name: The Magi (Wise Men)

verses.note: Wise men from the east arrive in Jerusalem seeking 'he that is born King of the Jews,' having seen his star
Herod secretly questions them and sends them to Bethlehem, asking them to report back
The star leads them to the young child; they worship him and present gold, frankincense, and myrrh
Warned in a dream not to return to Herod, they depart another way

funFacts: Never numbered or named in the text — the tradition of 'three' wise men comes only from the three gifts listed (Matthew 2:11), not from the text stating a headcount. Kept as a collective tier rather than named individuals for that reason.

characters.name: Herod the Great

verses.note: Troubled by the Magi's news, secretly questions them and the chief priests/scribes about the Christ's birthplace
Orders the slaughter of every male child in Bethlehem two years old and under, after the Magi don't return to him
His death is reported to Joseph in Egypt, in a dream, clearing the way for the family's return

funFacts: NAMING COLLISION, flagged rather than merged: this is Herod the Great, not the 'Herod the tetrarch' of Matthew 14 who executes John the Baptist — that is his son, Herod Antipas, kept as a separate submanager entry under John the Baptist's own tier rather than duplicated here.

characters.name: Simon Peter

verses.note: Called with his brother Andrew while casting a net into the sea of Galilee — 'Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men'
Steps out of the boat to walk on water toward Jesus, then begins to sink
Confesses 'Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God' — Jesus responds 'upon this rock I will build my church'
Present at the Transfiguration
Declares he will never deny Jesus, even if all others do
Denies Jesus three times before the cock crows, then weeps bitterly

funFacts: Promoted to his own full manager tier rather than staying grouped with the other apostles — same 'supporting ≠ minor' test used for Hur in Exodus: remove Peter from the confession, the water-walking, and the denial, and Matthew's whole portrait of faltering-but-real faith loses its central case study.

characters.name: Matthew (the Publican)

verses.note: Called by Jesus while 'sitting at the receipt of custom' as a tax collector
Hosts Jesus for a meal with 'many publicans and sinners,' drawing criticism from the Pharisees
Named among the twelve apostles, explicitly still called 'Matthew the publican' in his own list

funFacts: Traditionally credited as the author of this Gospel — chosen as the manager for this tier of remaining apostles both for his own real narrative beat (a tax collector, a genuinely disreputable profession to first-century Jewish readers, called and immediately celebrated) and as a fitting anchor for the book that bears his name.

characters.name: Judas Iscariot

verses.note: Named among the Twelve, already identified as 'who also betrayed him'
Agrees with the chief priests to betray Jesus for thirty pieces of silver
Identifies Jesus to the arresting crowd with a kiss
Overcome with remorse, returns the silver, and hangs himself

funFacts: Matthew is the only Gospel that records both the exact price (thirty pieces of silver, echoing Zechariah 11:12) and Judas's own death by his own hand afterward.

characters.name: Caiaphas

verses.note: The chief priests and elders gather 'unto the palace of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas' to plot against Jesus
Presides over the night trial before the Sanhedrin; tears his clothes when Jesus affirms he is the Christ, the Son of God, declaring it blasphemy
Formally puts the death sentence to the council — 'He is guilty of death'

funFacts: The only formally named high priest given a real decision-making role in Matthew's trial narrative — the recurring 'Pharisees and Sadducees' as a bloc are attached to this same tier as submanagers, since they oppose Jesus throughout the book without ever being individually named.

characters.name: Pontius Pilate

verses.note: Questions Jesus directly — 'Art thou the King of the Jews?' — marvels that Jesus answers nothing to the accusations
Offers to release either Jesus or Barabbas per a Passover custom; the crowd chooses Barabbas
Washes his hands before the crowd — 'I am innocent of the blood of this just person' — then delivers Jesus to be crucified
Grants the chief priests a guard to seal Jesus's tomb

funFacts: Matthew is the only Gospel that records his wife's dream-warning and his own hand-washing — both unique details not found in Mark, Luke, or John's accounts of the same trial.

verses.note: Found with child of the Holy Ghost before she and Joseph came together; he takes her as his wife on the angel's word
The Magi find 'the young child with Mary his mother' and worship him

characters.name: Joseph (husband of Mary)
characters.perkNote: Jesus's legal/adoptive father, not biological — the text is explicit that Mary was found with child of the Holy Ghost before he and Mary came together (Matthew 1:18-20). Kept off Jesus's genealogy.father field for that reason; the relationship is captured here instead.

verses.note: Minded to put Mary away privily, then obeys an angel's instruction in a dream to take her as his wife
Warned in a dream to flee to Egypt with Mary and Jesus to escape Herod
Warned again to return, and again to settle in Nazareth instead of Judaea

funFacts: Never once recorded speaking a single word in any Gospel — every instruction he receives and acts on comes through a dream, and he simply obeys.

characters.name: Herod Antipas ("Herod the tetrarch")
characters.perkNote: NAMING COLLISION: son of Herod the Great (his own separate tier, Matthew 2), not the same man. Attached here rather than given his own tier because his entire role in Matthew is about John the Baptist's death specifically.

verses.note: Had imprisoned John for condemning his marriage to Herodias, his brother Philip's wife; wanted to kill him but feared the multitude
Grants Herodias' daughter's request for John's head on a charger, after a rash oath made at his own birthday feast
Herod Antipas's unlawfully-married wife; instructs her daughter to ask for John's head
Peter's brother, called together with him while casting a net into the sea
Named second among the twelve apostles, immediately after Peter
Called with his brother John while mending nets in their father Zebedee's boat
Present at the Transfiguration with Peter and John
His mother asks Jesus that he and John sit at Jesus's right and left hand in his kingdom

characters.name: John (son of Zebedee)

verses.note: Called with his brother James while mending nets
Present at the Transfiguration

funFacts: Not to be confused with John the Baptist, his own major tier in this same book — two different men named John.

verses.note: Named among the twelve apostles
Named among the twelve apostles

characters.name: Thomas

verses.note: Named among the twelve apostles

funFacts: His famous doubt at the resurrection is a John's-Gospel scene, not Matthew's — kept to what this specific book actually records (his name in the apostle list only).

characters.name: James (son of Alphaeus)

verses.note: Named among the twelve apostles

funFacts: A different man from Matthew himself, even though Mark 2:14 separately calls Matthew/Levi 'the son of Alphaeus' too — flagged as a possible identity question the text doesn't resolve, not silently merged.

verses.note: Named among the twelve apostles under this double name

characters.name: Simon the Canaanite

verses.note: Named among the twelve apostles

funFacts: Not to be confused with Simon Peter, Simon of Cyrene, or Simon the leper — several different Simons appear across this one Gospel, a very common first-century name.

characters.name: The Pharisees
characters.perkNote: Recurring opposition bloc, never individually named in Matthew — attached as a collective rather than inventing individual names the text doesn't give.

verses.note: Take counsel against Jesus to destroy him after a Sabbath healing
Subject of Jesus's extended 'woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites' discourse

characters.name: The Sadducees
characters.perkNote: Same treatment as the Pharisees — a recurring named class, never individuated in the text.

verses.note: Question Jesus about the resurrection, 'which say that there is no resurrection'
A 'notable prisoner' released instead of Jesus at the crowd's demand

characters.name: Pilate's Wife

verses.note: Sends word to Pilate during the trial: 'Have thou nothing to do with that just man: for I have suffered many things this day in a dream because of him'

funFacts: Never named in Matthew itself — later tradition calls her Claudia Procula, but that name isn't in this text, so she's kept here as 'Pilate's Wife.'

characters.name: The Sermon on the Mount
characters.purpose: Opens with the Beatitudes and moves through the Lord's Prayer, teaching on anger, adultery, oaths, retaliation, love of enemies, giving, prayer, fasting, treasure, worry, judging others, and the wise/foolish builders. The core statement of Kingdom ethics in Matthew — what it actually looks like to live under God's reign, not just believe in it.

verses.note: The full sermon, delivered on a mountain to his disciples with the multitudes also hearing

characters.name: The Parables of the Kingdom
characters.purpose: A chapter of short earthly stories (the sower, the wheat and tares, the mustard seed, the leaven, the hidden treasure, the pearl of great price, the net) each illustrating some facet of what the Kingdom of Heaven is like — deliberately indirect teaching, explained privately to the disciples but left as riddles to the crowd.

verses.note: Seven parables plus Jesus's own explanation of why he teaches in parables (13:10-17)

characters.name: The Olivet Discourse
characters.purpose: Delivered privately on the Mount of Olives in response to the disciples asking when the temple's destruction and his coming would be — signs of the end, the parable of the fig tree, and the closing parables of readiness (the ten virgins, the talents, the sheep and the goats). Teaches watchfulness rather than date-setting.

verses.note: The full discourse, given just before the Passion narrative begins

characters.name: The Great Commission
characters.purpose: The risen Jesus's final recorded words in this Gospel, given to the eleven remaining disciples on a mountain in Galilee — a direct charge to make disciples of all nations, baptizing and teaching, closing with the promise 'lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world.' The book's own closing thesis: what all of it was for.

verses.note: The final verses of the book
Present at the crucifixion and burial
One of the two women who find the empty tomb and are first told Jesus is risen
Named alongside Mary Magdalene at the crucifixion, burial, and empty tomb — likely the mother of James and Joses per 27:56, not individually indexed further here
A rich man and Jesus's disciple who requests the body from Pilate and buries it in his own new tomb
Compelled to carry Jesus's cross

genealogyLists.note: Bulk or deliberately-unresolved references, kept out of the character list above.

jesusGenealogy.note: Abraham to Jesus in three sets of fourteen generations. Almost entirely OT figures already indexed in Genesis/Ruth/1&2 Samuel/1&2 Kings/1&2 Chronicles — not re-indexed here to avoid duplicating those books' own character entries. Notable feature: four women are named in a genealogy that otherwise lists only men — Tamar, Rahab, Ruth, and 'her that had been the wife of Urias' (Bathsheba, not named directly here) — each with an unconventional or Gentile background, worth flagging as deliberate rather than incidental.

chiefPriestsAndScribes.note: Consulted by Herod the Great about where the Christ should be born — never individually named, kept as a bulk reference rather than invented individuals.

theCenturionAtTheCross.note: Unnamed — 'Truly this was the Son of God' — along with those watching with him.
